title: Accelerating ab initio melting property calculations with machine learning: application to the high entropy alloy TaVCrW

recollection.starting_material: Guess: An equiatomic Ta–V–Cr–W refractory high-entropy alloy modeled as a random bcc solid solution (e.g., SQS supercells) with both solid and liquid configurations sampled for training/validation.
recollection.intervention: Guess: Train a machine-learning interatomic potential on DFT (ab initio) data across solid and liquid states using active learning, then use it to run large-scale MD (two-phase coexistence and/or free-energy thermodynamic integration) to compute the melting curve and related thermodynamic properties; validate against smaller-scale ab initio MD.
recollection.structure: Guess: A chemically disordered bcc solid solution coexisting with a metallic liquid; the solid remains bcc up to melting with minimal long-range order and only weak chemical short-range order; upon heating, a solid–liquid interface is stabilized to locate Tm.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: The ML potential reproduces ab initio energetics/forces for chemically disordered, anharmonic configurations, enabling statistically converged solid–liquid coexistence simulations; melting is governed by the balance of mixing enthalpy with vibrational and configurational entropies, with pressure dependence set by the solid–liquid volume change; the ML model accelerates sampling while retaining ab initio accuracy.
recollection.results: Guess: Ambient-pressure melting temperature Tm ≈ 3000 ± 100 K (on the order of 2.9–3.2 kK); latent heat of fusion ~0.45–0.6 eV/atom; volume expansion on melting ~2–4%; Clapeyron slope dTm/dP ~25–35 K/GPa. The ML potential attains energy MAE of a few meV/atom and force MAE ~50–80 meV/Å relative to DFT, delivering ~10^3–10^4× speedup. Predicted Tm agrees with direct ab initio estimates within ~50–100 K.

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies a DFT-trained ML interatomic potential and a disordered BCC TaVCrW solid/liquid setting, but only generically. It misses the specific MTP-for-liquid and FEP-instead-of-TI strategy, the <1 meV/atom phase-space fidelity, and the key electronic-excitation and SRO mechanisms. Its coexistence/TI description is inconsistent with the central method, and its numerical predictions do not match the reported 80% savings, 193/160 K CALPHAD offsets, 48/57 K electronic shifts, or 2.4 meV/atom SRO stabilization.
